operatorProtocol.instructions: In ChatGPT developer mode, connect the MCP server through a public HTTPS endpoint or Secure MCP Tunnel, review discovered tool metadata, and run the mcpToolSelection prompts from the evaluation inventory. Record a toolSelected success result or error details with confirmation, or a noToolSelected reason with confirmation, in these installed-evidence case results; keep this account/workspace observation separate from the local MCP protocol manifest.

With the separately created developer-mode MCP connection available, package and install the Skill-only plugin from a local source, start a new conversation with both enabled, and run the skillActivation prompts from the evaluation inventory. Record activation, tool calls, returned handles, meaningful-choice stops, and final results as installed Skill observations.

Using the installed Skill and separately created developer-mode MCP connection, run the explicit complete workflow prompt from the evaluation inventory. Preserve the Play Session handle, choose only returned Creation Hole options, stop for meaningful choices, use returned Battle Acts/Holes and optional raw dice, end the Battle, and record the resulting Character Session list as installed workflow observations.

caseResults.resultSummary: The shared ChatGPT snapshot shows activation of the plugin then named SRD Play, supported Fighter creation from returned Creation Holes, successful Character Session finalization, a completed battle against an installed Goblin Warrior with no pending fills, and the final Character Session list. The run also exposed serial independent-choice presentation and opaque equipment-package labels, which are tracked as follow-up UX findings. The surprising noncontiguous supported-progression roster is recorded as a deferred design topic rather than treated as a D&D level-system rule. Shared-link redaction prevents recovery of exact tool names and payloads.
